title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 10 questions (10.1, 10.2)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: HR sends email addresses in mixed case, such as Jane.DOE@Example.com, and the business wants every identity's email stored in lower case. Which transform BEST meets this need?
choices: lower
upper
normalizeNames
trim
questions.answer: lower
questions.explanation: The lower transform converts the whole input string to lower case. normalizeNames capitalizes name parts, which is the opposite of what is needed.

questions.stem: An account create profile must build a username from the first letter of the first name plus the full last name, all in lower case, such as jsmith. Which combination of transforms BEST fits?
choices: substring for the first letter, concat to join it with the last name, and lower around the result
leftPad the first name, concat it with the last name, and trim around the result
lookup the first letter, firstValid to add the last name, and lower around the result
split on the first letter, replace to join it with the last name, and upper around the result
questions.answer: substring for the first letter, concat to join it with the last name, and lower around the result
questions.explanation: substring takes the first character, concat joins the parts and lower normalizes case. lookup and firstValid do not extract or join characters.

questions.stem: A phone attribute holds values such as (555) 123-4567. An engineer applies {"type": "replace", "attributes": {"regex": "[^0-9]", "replacement": ""}}. What is the output?
choices: The string 5551234567
The string (555)1234567
The string 555 123 4567
The string (555) 123-4567
questions.answer: The string 5551234567
questions.explanation: replace substitutes every match of the regex, and [^0-9] matches every character that is not a digit, so only the digits remain. The other outputs keep characters the regex removes.

questions.stem: A target system needs employee numbers as exactly eight characters with leading zeros, so 4512 becomes 00004512. Which transform BEST does this?
choices: rightPad with a length of 8 and a padding of 0
leftPad with a length of 8 and a padding of 0
substring with a begin of 0 and an end of 8
concat with the static value 0000 in front
questions.answer: leftPad with a length of 8 and a padding of 0
questions.explanation: leftPad adds the padding character on the left until the value reaches the set length. A static prefix of four zeros only works for four-digit numbers.

questions.stem: An engineer splits Smith, John on the comma and takes index 1 to get the first name, but the result has a leading space. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Change the split index from 1 to 0
Wrap the split transform in a trim transform
Add a leftPad transform with a length of 4
Replace the split transform with a lower transform
questions.answer: Wrap the split transform in a trim transform
questions.explanation: trim removes leading and trailing whitespace from the split result. Index 0 would return the last name instead.

questions.stem: Usernames must not contain accents, so the first name José should be used as Jose. Which transform BEST meets this need?
choices: e164phone
decomposeDiacriticalMarks
base64Encode
normalizeNames
questions.answer: decomposeDiacriticalMarks
questions.explanation: decomposeDiacriticalMarks replaces accented characters with their plain equivalents. normalizeNames fixes capitalization but keeps the accents.

questions.stem: A department value must have several different substitutions in one step: & to and, / to a hyphen, and runs of spaces to one space. Which transform BEST fits?
choices: conditional with one expression for each substitution
replaceAll with a table of regex patterns and their replacements
lookup with a table of every possible department name
replace with one regex that matches all three cases
questions.answer: replaceAll with a table of regex patterns and their replacements
questions.explanation: replaceAll applies a table of pattern and replacement pairs in a single transform. A single replace can only apply one replacement value to every match.

questions.stem: An engineer applies {"type": "substring", "attributes": {"begin": 0, "end": 3}} to the department value Marketing. What is the output?
choices: Mark
ark
Mar
Marketing
questions.answer: Mar
questions.explanation: begin is a zero-based start index and end is exclusive, so characters at positions 0, 1 and 2 are returned. Mark would need an end of 4.

questions.stem: Office location codes such as NYC1 and LON2 must become region names, and any code not in the list must become Unassigned. Which transform BEST fits?
choices: replace with a regex that matches each office code
conditional with one expression for each office code
firstValid with a list of region names and a static fallback value
lookup with a table of codes and a default entry of Unassigned
questions.answer: lookup with a table of codes and a default entry of Unassigned
questions.explanation: lookup maps input values through a table, and its default entry covers values that have no match. firstValid only picks the first non-null value from a list.

questions.stem: A lookup transform maps country codes to names but has no default entry. An identity arrives with a code that is not in the table. What happens?
choices: The transform returns an error for that identity
The first value in the table is returned
An empty string is returned with no error
The original code is passed through unchanged
questions.answer: The transform returns an error for that identity
questions.explanation: Without a default entry, an input that matches no key causes the lookup to error. Adding a default key is the safe design.

questions.stem: An engineer wants a conditional transform to output Senior when an identity's salary band is greater than 7. Why will a conditional transform not express this directly?
choices: The conditional transform must always output a number
The conditional transform only works on date values
The conditional transform cannot read any account attributes
The conditional transform only supports the eq comparison
questions.answer: The conditional transform only supports the eq comparison
questions.explanation: The conditional expression compares two values with eq only, so greater-than logic needs another approach such as a static transform with a Velocity template. Its inputs can be any string.

questions.stem: A transform is {"type": "conditional", "attributes": {"expression": "$dept eq Sales", "positiveCondition": "SLS", "negativeCondition": "GEN", "dept": <accountAttribute for department>}}. An identity's department is Finance. What is the output?
choices: GEN
SLS
Sales
Finance
questions.answer: GEN
questions.explanation: Finance does not equal Sales, so the expression is false and the negativeCondition value is returned. SLS is only returned when the department is Sales.

questions.stem: An identity's email should come from the HR source's workEmail if present, otherwise from Active Directory's mail, otherwise a placeholder. Which transform BEST fits?
choices: conditional comparing HR workEmail with AD mail using eq
lookup with HR workEmail as the key and AD mail as the default
firstValid with HR workEmail, then AD mail, then a static placeholder
concat with HR workEmail, AD mail and the placeholder joined together
questions.answer: firstValid with HR workEmail, then AD mail, then a static placeholder
questions.explanation: firstValid returns the first value in its list that is not null, in the order given. concat would join all three values into one string.

questions.stem: An employee type must map to three different outputs, with extra logic when the type is empty, and the engineer wants one readable transform. Which approach BEST fits?
choices: A substring transform with three begin and end values
A dateCompare transform with three separate positiveCondition values
A reference transform pointing at three saved transforms
A static transform with a Velocity template using #if and #elseif
questions.answer: A static transform with a Velocity template using #if and #elseif
questions.explanation: A static transform evaluates a Velocity template, which supports multi-branch #if logic over variables defined as nested transforms. dateCompare only compares dates.

questions.stem: A firstValid transform lists three nested transforms. For some identities the first nested transform throws an error because its input is missing. What setting lets firstValid move on to the next value?
choices: Set the default entry to true on the firstValid transform
Set accountSortDescending to true on the nested transform
Set ignoreErrors to true on the firstValid transform
Set requiresPeriodicRefresh to true on the firstValid transform
questions.answer: Set ignoreErrors to true on the firstValid transform
questions.explanation: ignoreErrors tells firstValid to skip a value whose transform errors and try the next one. requiresPeriodicRefresh only controls nightly reevaluation.

questions.stem: HR sends hire dates as 03/15/2024 and the identity attribute must be stored in ISO8601. Which transform configuration BEST fits?
choices: dateCompare with a firstDate of the hire date and a secondDate of now
dateMath with an expression of now and rounding to the day
dateFormat with an inputFormat of ISO8601 and an outputFormat of MM/dd/yyyy
dateFormat with an inputFormat of MM/dd/yyyy and an outputFormat of ISO8601
questions.answer: dateFormat with an inputFormat of MM/dd/yyyy and an outputFormat of ISO8601
questions.explanation: dateFormat converts a date from its inputFormat into its outputFormat. The reversed formats would fail to parse the HR value.

questions.stem: A lifecycle state should be inactive once an identity's end date is earlier than today and active otherwise. Which transform BEST evaluates this?
choices: dateFormat with the end date as input and an outputFormat set to the word now
dateCompare with firstDate as the end date, secondDate as now and LT
conditional with an expression of $endDate eq now
dateMath with the end date as input and an expression of now
questions.answer: dateCompare with firstDate as the end date, secondDate as now and LT
questions.explanation: dateCompare compares two dates with an operator and returns positiveCondition or negativeCondition; now can be the second date. conditional only checks equality and would not compare dates.

questions.stem: A lifecycle transform uses dateCompare against now. Identities whose end date passed last week still show active because nothing changed on the HR record. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Set ignoreErrors to true on the dateCompare transform
Run an entitlement aggregation on the HR source every night
Change the operator from LT to GTE on the dateCompare transform it uses
Set requiresPeriodicRefresh to true so it is reevaluated nightly
questions.answer: Set requiresPeriodicRefresh to true so it is reevaluated nightly
questions.explanation: Transforms that depend on the current date need requiresPeriodicRefresh so they are reevaluated during the nightly identity refresh. Changing the operator would invert the logic.

questions.stem: A provisioning policy must set an account's expiration to 30 days after the identity's start date. Which transform BEST computes the new date?
choices: dateMath with the start date as input and an expression of +30d
dateCompare with the start date and an operator of GT
dateFormat with an outputFormat that adds thirty days
leftPad with the start date and a length of 30
questions.answer: dateMath with the start date as input and an expression of +30d
questions.explanation: dateMath adds or subtracts time from a date using expressions such as +30d. dateFormat only changes how a date is written.

questions.stem: Which comparison operators does the dateCompare transform support?
choices: before, after and equals
LT and GT only
LT, LTE, GT and GTE
eq and ne only
questions.answer: LT, LTE, GT and GTE
questions.explanation: dateCompare uses LT, LTE, GT and GTE to compare its two dates. eq is the comparison used by the conditional transform.

questions.stem: A dateFormat transform with an outputFormat of yyyy-mm-dd produces values like 2024-00-15 and 2024-37-15. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Lower-case dd means day of the week, so it should be DD
ISO8601 input dates can never be written out in any custom date format
Lower-case mm means minutes, so the month pattern should be MM
The year pattern yyyy needs to be written as YYYY
questions.answer: Lower-case mm means minutes, so the month pattern should be MM
questions.explanation: Date patterns follow Java formatting, where MM is the month and mm is minutes. DD would be the day of the year, which is also wrong.

questions.stem: An identity attribute needs the Active Directory accountExpires value, which AD stores as a Windows file-time number, shown as a readable ISO8601 date. Which approach BEST fits?
choices: A substring transform that keeps the first eight digits
A lookup transform with a table of known expiry values
A dateFormat transform using its built-in Windows epoch input format
A dateMath transform that subtracts the Windows epoch
questions.answer: A dateFormat transform using its built-in Windows epoch input format
questions.explanation: dateFormat has named input formats for common epoch styles, including the Windows file-time format, and can output ISO8601. substring cannot convert a time count into a date.

questions.stem: An identity profile mapping uses {"type": "accountAttribute", "attributes": {"sourceName": "Workday", "attributeName": "LOCATION"}}. What does this transform return?
choices: The LOCATION value from the identity's account on the Workday source
The LOCATION value from every source the identity has accounts on
The name of the Workday source joined with the LOCATION value
The LOCATION identity attribute that was already calculated for the identity
questions.answer: The LOCATION value from the identity's account on the Workday source
questions.explanation: accountAttribute reads the named attribute from the identity's account on the named source. Reading an identity attribute is the job of identityAttribute.

questions.stem: Some identities have two accounts on the same source, and accountAttribute keeps returning a value from the older account. How can the engineer make it use the newest account?
choices: Set accountReturnFirstLink to false so no account is chosen
Set accountSortDescending to true so accounts are sorted newest first
Set requiresPeriodicRefresh to true so the newest account is always read
Set ignoreErrors to true so the older account is skipped
questions.answer: Set accountSortDescending to true so accounts are sorted newest first
questions.explanation: By default accounts are sorted by created date ascending, so the oldest is used; accountSortDescending reverses this. ignoreErrors belongs to firstValid.

questions.stem: Why should an engineer avoid the identityAttribute transform inside another identity attribute's mapping on an identity profile?
choices: identityAttribute can only read attributes that come from authoritative sources
identityAttribute only works inside SoD policy definitions
identityAttribute always returns the value in upper case
Attributes are calculated in parallel, so the value may be stale or missing
questions.answer: Attributes are calculated in parallel, so the value may be stale or missing
questions.explanation: Identity attribute calculation is multi-threaded, so referencing one identity attribute from another can read stale or missing data and cause exceptions. It is intended for account create and disable profiles.

questions.stem: An account create profile must set a new account's manager email field to the email address of the identity's manager. Which transform BEST fits?
choices: lookup with a table that maps each manager to an email address
getReferenceIdentityAttribute with uid set to manager and attributeName set to email
accountAttribute with sourceName set to manager and attributeName set to email
identityAttribute with name set to manager and a lower transform around it
questions.answer: getReferenceIdentityAttribute with uid set to manager and attributeName set to email
questions.explanation: getReferenceIdentityAttribute, a rule-type transform that calls the Cloud Services Deployment Utility rule, reads an attribute from another identity, and the special uid value manager points at the identity's manager. accountAttribute reads accounts on a source, not another identity.

questions.stem: Several identity profiles must use the same complex email-building transform, and the engineer wants one definition to maintain. Which transform type lets other transforms reuse it?
choices: firstValid, with the saved transform as its only value
static, with its value set to the saved transform's name
concat, with the saved transform as its first value
reference, with its id set to the saved transform's name
questions.answer: reference, with its id set to the saved transform's name
questions.explanation: The reference transform calls an existing saved transform by its id, which is the transform's name. static would only output that name as text.

questions.stem: A lower transform has no input attribute and is selected on an identity profile mapping for the HR source's email field. What value does it lower-case?
choices: Nothing, because input is required on every transform
The identity's current email identity attribute
The first attribute of the first account the identity has on any source
The source attribute chosen for that mapping in the identity profile
questions.answer: The source attribute chosen for that mapping in the identity profile
questions.explanation: When input is not given, the transform uses the source and attribute combination configured in the UI mapping. The input attribute is optional.

questions.stem: A transform is {"type": "lower", "attributes": {"input": {"type": "concat", "attributes": {"values": ["Jane", ".", "DOE"]}}}}. What is the output?
choices: j.doe
jane . doe
jane.doe
janedoe
questions.answer: jane.doe
questions.explanation: The nested concat runs first and builds Jane.DOE, then lower converts the whole result to lower case. Nested transforms are evaluated from the inside out.

questions.stem: During identity processing, the cost center must be fetched live from a finance REST API that the tenant does not aggregate. What is the BEST design?
choices: Aggregate the finance data as a source and read it with accountAttribute
Write an Identity Attribute cloud rule that calls the REST API
Use a static transform with a Velocity template that calls the finance API
Write a transform that calls the finance REST API directly
questions.answer: Aggregate the finance data as a source and read it with accountAttribute
questions.explanation: Transforms and cloud rules cannot call external systems, so the data must be aggregated into the tenant and read from the account. Cloud rules have no external connectivity.

questions.stem: An account create profile must generate a unique sAMAccountName, trying jsmith, then jsmith1, jsmith2 and so on. Which transform is built for this?
choices: lookup
usernameGenerator
randomAlphaNumeric
firstValid
questions.answer: usernameGenerator
questions.explanation: usernameGenerator tries a list of patterns with a unique counter and checks uniqueness, and it is used in account create profiles. randomAlphaNumeric makes random strings with no naming pattern.

questions.stem: An engineer changed a transform used on an identity profile and wants to see its effect on a sample identity before applying it to everyone. What should the engineer use?
choices: A test certification campaign for the identity
The Campaign Composition report
A delta aggregation on the authoritative source
The identity profile's preview for a selected identity
questions.answer: The identity profile's preview for a selected identity
questions.explanation: The identity profile preview shows the calculated attribute values for a chosen identity before changes are applied. Aggregations and campaigns do not preview transform output.

questions.stem: An engineer created a transform through the API, but no identity attributes changed. What is the MOST likely missing step?
choices: Upload the transform to the virtual appliance
Use it in an identity profile mapping and save the profile
Restart the virtual appliance cluster
Submit the transform to SailPoint support for a rule review
questions.answer: Use it in an identity profile mapping and save the profile
questions.explanation: A saved transform does nothing until it is used in a mapping or policy, and saving the identity profile processes identities. Transforms are not reviewed by SailPoint like cloud rules.

questions.stem: Which requirement is MOST likely to need a rule instead of the built-in transforms?
choices: Changing a department value to lower case
Mapping location codes to region names, with a default for unknown codes
Looping over each value of a multi-valued attribute with custom logic
Converting a hire date from MM/dd/yyyy to ISO8601
questions.answer: Looping over each value of a multi-valued attribute with custom logic
questions.explanation: Custom per-item logic over a multi-valued attribute goes beyond the fixed operations of the built-in transforms, so it is the requirement most likely to need a rule. The other three are each a single built-in transform.

questions.stem: A target system needs phone numbers in E.164 format, such as +15551234567, from values entered in many local styles. What is the simplest approach?
choices: A leftPad transform that adds a plus sign
A cloud rule that parses every phone format
The e164phone transform with a default region
A lookup transform with a table of known phone numbers
questions.answer: The e164phone transform with a default region
questions.explanation: e164phone formats phone numbers to E.164, using its defaultRegion (US unless set) when no country code is present, and returns null for input that is not a valid phone number. A rule would add review effort for something a built-in transform does.

questions.stem: In the Admin UI, where does an engineer select a saved transform to calculate an identity attribute?
choices: The Mappings tab of the identity profile
The Account Schema tab of the source
The Accounts tab of the identity's details
The Controls page of an SoD policy
questions.answer: The Mappings tab of the identity profile
questions.explanation: Saved transforms are applied to identity attributes on the identity profile's Mappings tab (Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles), where the result can then be previewed. Account schemas, identity details and SoD controls do not apply transforms.

questions.stem: Match each data requirement to the transform that BEST fits it.

pairs.item: Use HR email if present, otherwise AD mail
Map office codes to region names with a fallback
Read the manager's email for a create profile

questions.explanation: Each requirement is a single built-in operation. dateCompare compares two dates and is not needed for any of these requirements.

questions.stem: Put the steps for building and rolling out a date-based lifecycle state transform in order.
items: Read the end date with an accountAttribute transform
Convert the end date to ISO8601 with a dateFormat transform
Compare it with now using a dateCompare transform
Set requiresPeriodicRefresh so it is reevaluated nightly
Preview the result on a sample identity in the identity profile
questions.explanation: The value is read, normalized, then compared; the nightly refresh flag keeps the result current, and a preview confirms the output before rollout.

questions.stem: An engineer is reviewing an identity profile that uses transforms. Which TWO statements are correct?
choices: Without an input attribute, a transform uses the mapping's source attribute
accountSortDescending makes accountAttribute choose the newest account
identityAttribute is the preferred way to chain identity attributes on a profile
The conditional transform supports greater-than comparisons
A lookup with no default returns its input when no key matches
answers: Without an input attribute, a transform uses the mapping's source attribute
accountSortDescending makes accountAttribute choose the newest account
questions.explanation: Implicit input and account sorting behave as stated. identityAttribute is not for identity profile chaining, conditional supports eq only and a lookup with no match and no default errors.

questions.stem: An engineer is documenting a JDBC Provision rule. Where do connector rules like this one run?
choices: In the multi-tenant cloud
Inside the IdentityIQ server
On the virtual appliance
On each reviewer's browser
questions.answer: On the virtual appliance
questions.explanation: Connector rules run on the virtual appliance as extensions of the connector. Cloud rules are the ones that run in the multi-tenant cloud.

questions.stem: An engineer wants an Identity Attribute rule to call an external HR API to fetch a value during identity processing. Why will this fail review?
choices: Identity Attribute rules run on the virtual appliance, which has no internet access
Identity Attribute rules can only be written in PowerShell
External calls are allowed but must use System.out for logging
Cloud rules run in the multi-tenant cloud and may not make external connections
questions.answer: Cloud rules run in the multi-tenant cloud and may not make external connections
questions.explanation: Cloud rules have a restricted context with no external connectivity. Identity Attribute rules are BeanShell cloud rules, not PowerShell or appliance rules.

questions.stem: A Web Services After Operation rule needs to look up an identity's attributes in the tenant's data model. Why is this not possible?
choices: Connector rules cannot query the tenant's data model; they use the context sent
Connector rules must first be approved by the manager of every affected identity
Connector rules can only read data from delimited files
Connector rules can only run during certification campaigns
questions.answer: Connector rules cannot query the tenant's data model; they use the context sent
questions.explanation: Connector rules run on the appliance without access to the platform data model and use the context sent to them. They may use the managed connection provided, but not extra call-outs.

questions.stem: An engineer is classifying the rules used in a tenant. Which of these rules is a cloud rule?
choices: Web Services Before Operation rule
JDBC Provision rule
Before Provisioning rule
Before Creation rule for Active Directory
questions.answer: Before Provisioning rule
questions.explanation: Before Provisioning runs in the cloud before a plan is sent to a source. The others are connector rules that run on the appliance or IQService.

questions.stem: An AD team needs a PowerShell script to create a home directory after each new account is created. Which kind of rule fits?
choices: An After Creation connector rule that runs through IQService
An Identity Attribute cloud rule on the HR identity profile
A Correlation cloud rule on the Active Directory source
A Before Provisioning cloud rule that runs in the tenant
questions.answer: An After Creation connector rule that runs through IQService
questions.explanation: After Creation rules run PowerShell on the IQService component after an AD account is created. Cloud rules cannot run commands on the customer's servers.

questions.stem: How does an engineer deploy a new Web Services Before Operation rule to the tenant?
choices: Copy it to the virtual appliance file system and restart the appliance
Email it to SailPoint support for a rule review and wait for deployment
Paste it into a transform as the value of a static transform
Upload it with the connector rule REST APIs, with no SailPoint review
questions.answer: Upload it with the connector rule REST APIs, with no SailPoint review
questions.explanation: Connector rules have no rule review process and are managed directly through the connector rule APIs, which check for harmful code. Cloud rules are the ones submitted for review.

questions.stem: A cloud rule's author wants it to save a change to an identity object while it runs. Why is this not allowed?
choices: Cloud rules may save objects only when written in PowerShell
Cloud rules may only save objects on the virtual appliance
Cloud rules may read the data model but cannot save objects
Cloud rules may only save objects while a certification campaign is running
questions.answer: Cloud rules may read the data model but cannot save objects
questions.explanation: Cloud rules can query the data model in a read-only way but cannot commit transactions or save objects. Where they run does not change that.

questions.stem: Account names on a legacy app look like a-jsmith, while the matching identities have a uid of jsmith. Standard correlation cannot strip the prefix. Which rule BEST fits?
choices: A JDBC BuildMap rule that deletes the prefix in the database
A Before Provisioning rule that renames each account on the app to remove it
A Correlation rule that strips the prefix and returns the attribute to match
A Manager Correlation rule that links each account to a manager
questions.answer: A Correlation rule that strips the prefix and returns the attribute to match
questions.explanation: A Correlation rule applies custom logic to link accounts to identities. Renaming accounts on the target changes data rather than correlating it.

questions.stem: HR stores each worker's manager as Last, First instead of an ID, so attribute-based manager correlation fails. Which rule BEST fits?
choices: JDBC Provision rule
Identity Attribute rule
Correlation rule
Manager Correlation rule
questions.answer: Manager Correlation rule
questions.explanation: A Manager Correlation rule calculates the manager relationship with custom logic. A Correlation rule links accounts to identities, not identities to managers.

questions.stem: Whenever an AD account is disabled, the engineer must also add a description change to the provisioning plan before it is sent. Which rule is designed for this?
choices: Before Provisioning rule
Manager Correlation rule
Identity Attribute rule
BuildMap rule
questions.answer: Before Provisioning rule
questions.explanation: Before Provisioning rules modify the provisioning plan before it reaches the source. Identity Attribute rules only calculate identity attributes.

questions.stem: A unique account ID must follow rules more complex than any username pattern, checking several values before choosing one. Which rule type fits an account create profile field?
choices: Account Profile Attribute Generator rule
Correlation rule
Before Creation rule
Web Services After Operation rule
questions.answer: Account Profile Attribute Generator rule
questions.explanation: Attribute Generator rules generate complex account attribute values during provisioning, such as account creation. Correlation rules match accounts to identities.

questions.stem: A database source must provision accounts by calling several stored procedures in a specific order. Which rule fits?
choices: Before Provisioning rule
JDBC Provision rule
JDBC BuildMap rule
Identity Attribute rule
questions.answer: JDBC Provision rule
questions.explanation: A JDBC Provision rule runs database statements to provision accounts and access. JDBC BuildMap shapes data during aggregation, not provisioning.

questions.stem: A REST API returns account data in a deeply nested structure that the Web Services connector's response mapping cannot parse. Which rule BEST fits?
choices: Manager Correlation rule
Before Provisioning rule
Web Services Before Operation rule
Web Services After Operation rule
questions.answer: Web Services After Operation rule
questions.explanation: After Operation rules run after an HTTP operation and are often used to parse complex responses. Before Operation rules prepare the request.

questions.stem: A JDBC source's query returns rows that must be reshaped, with an extra database call for each account, during aggregation. Which rule fits?
choices: JDBC BuildMap rule
JDBC Provision rule
Correlation rule
Account Profile Attribute Generator rule
questions.answer: JDBC BuildMap rule
questions.explanation: JDBC BuildMap calculates and transforms query results during aggregation and can call back to the database. JDBC Provision is for provisioning.

questions.stem: An engineer finds an old design that relies on a Certification Exclusion rule. What should replace it in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: A Before Provisioning rule on each source
A JDBC BuildMap rule that drops excluded rows
An Identity Attribute rule that flags excluded items
Configurable certification campaign filters
questions.answer: Configurable certification campaign filters
questions.explanation: Certification Exclusion rules are deprecated and replaced by campaign filters. Dropping rows during aggregation would hide the access from the tenant altogether.

questions.stem: An engineer is ready to submit a new Identity Attribute rule. What should the submission include?
choices: The rule file and the virtual appliance's keypair
The rule file and a screenshot of the identity profile
The rule, the validator output, the tenant name and Expert Services approval
The rule file and an org admin's personal access token
questions.answer: The rule, the validator output, the tenant name and Expert Services approval
questions.explanation: SailPoint asks for the rule, validator output, tenant name and approval for Expert Services through a support request. Credentials and keys must never be sent.

questions.stem: What does SailPoint check when it reviews a submitted cloud rule?
choices: That the rule passes the customer's own user acceptance tests
That the rule has been approved by the manager of each affected identity first
That the rule produces the business outcome the customer expects
That the rule meets SailPoint's coding, security and performance guidelines
questions.answer: That the rule meets SailPoint's coding, security and performance guidelines
questions.explanation: The review is an integrity check against guidelines and intended use; SailPoint does not verify that the rule works as expected. Testing the outcome remains the implementer's job.

questions.stem: A go-live needs a cloud rule deployed during a specific window on a Thursday. What should the implementer do?
choices: Upload the rule to the virtual appliance before the window
Give SailPoint at least 48 hours notice to reserve a reviewer and deployer
Deploy the rule personally through the connector rule APIs
Submit the rule on Thursday morning and ask SailPoint for it to be expedited
questions.answer: Give SailPoint at least 48 hours notice to reserve a reviewer and deployer
questions.explanation: Rule reviews have an SLA of about 24 hours, and SailPoint asks for 48 hours notice when a specific window is needed. Cloud rules cannot be self-deployed through the connector rule APIs.

questions.stem: A Correlation rule was approved and deployed in the sandbox tenant. How can the same rule reach production?
choices: Recreate the rule by hand in the production Admin UI
Paste the rule code into a transform in the production tenant and then save it
Promote it with the sp-config export and import APIs, since it is approved
Copy the rule file onto the production virtual appliance
questions.answer: Promote it with the sp-config export and import APIs, since it is approved
questions.explanation: Approved rules, including cloud rules, can be promoted from sandbox to production through sp-config because their signature was verified in review. Rebuilding the rule by hand would need another review.

questions.stem: An approved cloud rule needs changed logic, and the business wants full control over when the change goes live. What does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Submit a TEMP copy, apply and validate it in the window, then update the original
Edit the rule code directly in the tenant during the window
Disable the rule, wait a day, then submit the new logic
Submit a new rule with a version number in its name for each change
questions.answer: Submit a TEMP copy, apply and validate it in the window, then update the original
questions.explanation: The TEMP rule approach gives control over timing while keeping one rule per use case in the end. Keeping many versioned rules is not supported.

questions.stem: An implementer keeps a separate rule for every change, such as AD Rule v1, v2 and v3. Why is this a poor practice?
choices: Each tenant may hold only three rules of any one type
SailPoint expects one rule per use case, updated in place
Rules with numbers in their names fail the rule validator
Older versions of a rule are deleted when a new one is added
questions.answer: SailPoint expects one rule per use case, updated in place
questions.explanation: The guidance is to keep a single rule for a given use case and update it, which keeps reviews and support clear. Version numbers in names are not what fails validation.

questions.stem: Which file name follows SailPoint's naming convention for an IdentityAttribute rule called Calculate Lifecycle?
choices: Rule - IdentityAttribute - Calculate Lifecycle.xml
Calculate Lifecycle - Rule - IdentityAttribute.xml
IdentityAttribute_CalculateLifecycle.bsh
Rule-CalculateLifecycle-v1.json
questions.answer: Rule - IdentityAttribute - Calculate Lifecycle.xml
questions.explanation: The convention is Rule - {type} - {name}.xml, matching the rule's type and name attributes. Cloud rules are XML documents, not JSON or bare BeanShell files.

questions.stem: A rule deployed last year starts producing wrong values after a business change. Who is responsible for fixing the rule's logic?
choices: The virtual appliance vendor, because rules run on the appliance
The customer or implementer, because rules are treated as configuration
SailPoint support, because every deployed rule is a supported product feature
The rule review team, because they approved the rule
questions.answer: The customer or implementer, because rules are treated as configuration
questions.explanation: SailPoint supports the platform, not rule configurations, so rule behaviour is the customer's or implementer's responsibility. Review approval is not a guarantee of correct logic.

questions.stem: In which language are Identity Security Cloud rules written?
choices: Python
JavaScript
Java BeanShell
Apache Velocity
questions.answer: Java BeanShell
questions.explanation: Rules use Java BeanShell, a lightweight scripting language with Java-like syntax. Velocity is used in static transforms, not rules.

questions.stem: A rule contains if (dept == "Sales") where dept was read from an identity attribute, and the check never matches. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Use "Sales".equals(dept), which is safe when dept is null
Use dept = "Sales", which compares and assigns at the same time
Use dept.equals("Sales") without a null check, which is always safe
Use dept === "Sales", which forces a strict type comparison
questions.answer: Use "Sales".equals(dept), which is safe when dept is null
questions.explanation: == compares object references for strings, so .equals is needed, and calling it on the literal avoids a null pointer error. === is not BeanShell syntax and = is assignment.

questions.stem: An Identity Attribute rule calls identity.getAttribute("department").toUpperCase() and fails for some identities. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Identity attributes can only be read from inside connector rules on the appliance
toUpperCase is not available in BeanShell
Some identities have no department, so the call is made on a null value
getAttribute only works on attributes in upper case
questions.answer: Some identities have no department, so the call is made on a null value
questions.explanation: Calling a method on a null value throws a null pointer error, which is why guidelines require null checks. BeanShell supports standard Java string methods.

questions.stem: A rule author wants to record debugging output from a cloud rule. Which approach follows SailPoint's guidelines?
choices: Call .toXml() on each object and log the full output
Create a new Log4j logger at the top of the rule
Use System.out.println() so the output reaches the console and log files
Use log.debug() for debug details and log.error() only for real failures
questions.answer: Use log.debug() for debug details and log.error() only for real failures
questions.explanation: Rules should use the provided log object with the right level; System.out, custom loggers and full object serialization are prohibited. Console output is not collected by the log aggregators.

questions.stem: What should a Correlation rule return to link an account to an identity?
choices: The full identity object loaded from the tenant
The account's native identity as a plain string
A map naming the identity attribute and the value to match
A Boolean that says whether a match was found
questions.answer: A map naming the identity attribute and the value to match
questions.explanation: A Correlation rule returns a map with the identity attribute name and value used for matching. Returning a Boolean gives the platform nothing to match on.

questions.stem: Why is a cloud rule's BeanShell code usually placed inside a CDATA section in the rule XML?
choices: So the rule runs on the virtual appliance instead of the cloud
So characters such as < and & in the code do not need XML escaping
So the code is encrypted before it is stored in the tenant
So the rule can import classes that are otherwise blocked
questions.answer: So characters such as < and & in the code do not need XML escaping
questions.explanation: CDATA lets code with operators like < and && sit in the XML without escaping. It does not change where the rule runs or what it may import.

questions.stem: A submitted rule uses context.getObjectByName() to load an identity. The reviewer returns it. What should the author use instead?
choices: A REST call from the rule to the tenant's own API
A direct JDBC connection to the tenant's database
The helper methods of the SailPoint rule utility, available as idn
A Thread that loads the identity in the background while the rule waits
questions.answer: The helper methods of the SailPoint rule utility, available as idn
questions.explanation: Direct context calls are restricted, and new rules must use the rule utility helper methods instead. Direct connections, threads and call-outs are all prohibited.

questions.stem: A rule author wants to make sure an optional BeanShell variable was actually passed into the rule before using it. Which check is specific to BeanShell?
choices: Wrap the variable in Optional.of() before reading it
Call isEmpty() on the variable before any other check
Compare the variable with undefined, as in JavaScript
Compare the variable with void, which means it was never defined
questions.answer: Compare the variable with void, which means it was never defined
questions.explanation: In BeanShell an undefined variable has the special value void, so checking for void avoids errors. undefined is JavaScript, and Optional.of fails on null.

questions.stem: A Before Provisioning rule loops through every account in the tenant to check a value for each plan. Why will this likely be rejected?
choices: Before Provisioning rules may only read one attribute per run
Before Provisioning rules may not contain any loops at all
Before Provisioning rules may only run once per day
Iterating over lists of accounts or identities is prohibited
questions.answer: Iterating over lists of accounts or identities is prohibited
questions.explanation: Guidelines forbid iterating over lists of accounts or identities because it bloats caches; a targeted query should be used. Simple loops over small data are allowed.

questions.stem: What is SailPoint's general guidance on choosing between rules and other product features?
choices: Use rules for every identity attribute so that all logic sits in one place
Treat rules as a last resort and prefer features such as transforms
Use rules first because they are faster than product features
Use rules only on sources that have no virtual appliance
questions.answer: Treat rules as a last resort and prefer features such as transforms
questions.explanation: SailPoint recommends treating rules as a last resort because of review, support and performance implications. Transforms are configurable without a review.

questions.stem: A requirement is to store every identity's last name in upper case. An implementer proposes an Identity Attribute rule. What is the BEST response?
choices: Approve the rule, because rules are the standard for attributes
Use an upper transform, which needs no rule review
Use a Before Provisioning rule so the value is set at provisioning
Use a Correlation rule so the value is set when accounts link
questions.answer: Use an upper transform, which needs no rule review
questions.explanation: A built-in upper transform meets the need without the cost and delay of a rule review. A Correlation rule is unrelated to attribute formatting.

questions.stem: A transform needs logic that no built-in transform offers, so the engineer has a reviewed cloud rule. How does a transform call that rule?
choices: With {"type": "rule", "attributes": {"name": "<rule name>"}}
With {"type": "lookup", "attributes": {"table": "<rule name>"}}
With {"type": "reference", "attributes": {"id": "<rule name>"}}
With {"type": "static", "attributes": {"value": "<rule name>"}}
questions.answer: With {"type": "rule", "attributes": {"name": "<rule name>"}}
questions.explanation: The rule transform runs a cloud rule by name from inside a transform. reference calls another saved transform, not a rule.

questions.stem: An old design used an Identity Selector rule to decide who receives a role. What should be used instead?
choices: A lookup transform on the role's description
The role's standard membership criteria
A Correlation rule on the authoritative source
A Before Provisioning rule on each source in the role
questions.answer: The role's standard membership criteria
questions.explanation: Identity Selector rules are deprecated in favour of role standard assignment criteria. Before Provisioning rules change plans, not who gets a role.

questions.stem: A legacy integration used an Integration rule to modify provisioning requests. What is its replacement?
choices: A JDBC BuildMap rule
A Before Provisioning rule
A Manager Correlation rule
A dateMath transform
questions.answer: A Before Provisioning rule
questions.explanation: Integration rules are deprecated and replaced by Before Provisioning rules. BuildMap rules act during aggregation, not provisioning.

questions.stem: A region-to-office mapping changes almost every month. One implementer proposes a rule and another a lookup transform. Why is the transform the BETTER choice?
choices: Lookup transforms are reviewed by SailPoint, so they are safer
The team can update the transform at any time with no rule review
Rules cannot contain more than ten mapping values
Lookup transforms run on the virtual appliance, so they are always faster
questions.answer: The team can update the transform at any time with no rule review
questions.explanation: Transforms are maintained by the customer through the API or UI with no review cycle, so frequent changes are easy. Every change to a cloud rule needs another review.

questions.stem: Account usernames must be unique across AD and a second directory, using naming logic beyond any pattern list, and no built-in transform can express it. What is the BEST option?
choices: An Account Profile Attribute Generator rule reviewed by SailPoint
A JDBC Provision rule on the Active Directory source
A Manager Correlation rule on the HR source
A usernameGenerator transform with patterns for both of the directories
questions.answer: An Account Profile Attribute Generator rule reviewed by SailPoint
questions.explanation: When the logic goes beyond what transforms can express, an Attribute Generator rule is the right tool, after review. JDBC Provision rules only apply to JDBC sources.

questions.stem: Match each Identity Security Cloud rule to where it runs.

pairs.match: In the multi-tenant cloud before the plan is sent
On the virtual appliance with the JDBC connector

pairs.item: After Creation rule for Active Directory
pairs.match: On IQService as a PowerShell script
In the multi-tenant cloud during identity processing

targets_extra: In the reviewer's browser during certification
questions.explanation: Cloud rules run in the tenant's cloud, connector rules on the appliance, and AD native rules on IQService. No rule runs in a reviewer's browser.

questions.stem: Put the steps for delivering a new cloud rule in order.
items: Confirm that no transform or product feature meets the need
Write the rule and test its logic against sandbox data
Run the rule validator and fix any findings
Submit the rule, validator output and tenant name to SailPoint
Attach the approved rule and promote it to production with sp-config
questions.explanation: Rules are a last resort, so alternatives come first, then testing, validation, review and finally promotion of the approved rule.

questions.stem: A reviewer is checking a submitted cloud rule against SailPoint's guidelines. Which TWO items would cause it to be returned?
choices: Calling Thread.sleep() to wait for data
Logging an identity's password at debug level
Checking a variable for null before using it
Using log.warn() for a non-critical issue
Using "Sales".equals(dept) to compare strings
answers: Calling Thread.sleep() to wait for data
Logging an identity's password at debug level
questions.explanation: Sleeps and threads are prohibited, and logging sensitive data causes rejection. Null checks, correct log levels and .equals comparisons are good practice.
